title: Soong Build System
description: AOSP build: Android.bp, Blueprint, module types, lunch/m, Kati and Ninja.

questions.question: Which file does Soong read to define modules?
questions.explanation: Android.bp files use the Blueprint syntax. Android.mk files are still handled by Kati.

questions.question: What does Soong ultimately generate to execute the build?
questions.explanation: Soong (and Kati for .mk files) produce Ninja files; Ninja runs the actual build steps.

questions.question: Which statements about Blueprint (Android.bp) syntax are correct?

answers.text: Variant-specific settings use nested properties such as arch, target or product_variables
Arbitrary shell commands can be run while parsing the file

questions.explanation: Blueprint is declarative on purpose. Complex logic belongs in Go (Soong plugins) or soong_config_module_type.

questions.question: Which module type builds an APK?
questions.explanation: android_library builds an AAR-like library with resources; java_library builds a jar; cc_binary a native executable.

questions.question: How can several modules share common properties in Android.bp?
questions.explanation: Defaults modules are merged into the referencing module; lists are appended, scalars overridden.

questions.question: What do you need to set for a system app to use hidden platform APIs and run as privileged?
questions.explanation: privileged installs to priv-app; platform_apis compiles against the full platform; signature permissions need the platform certificate.

questions.question: Which commands build modules from the current directory?
questions.explanation: m builds targets from the top of the tree; mm the current dir; mmm given dirs. lunch only selects the target.

questions.question: Which build variants can you select with lunch?
questions.explanation: user = production, userdebug = like user but with root/debuggability, eng = development defaults.

questions.question: Which tools come with the AOSP tree for working with Android.bp files?
questions.explanation: androidmk does a best-effort conversion; complex makefile logic needs manual work.

questions.question: How can a module install into the vendor partition?
questions.explanation: Similar flags: product_specific, system_ext_specific, device_specific (odm).

questions.question: Where does Soong put intermediate build outputs?
questions.explanation: Installed files end up under out/target/product/<device>/; intermediates live in out/soong/.intermediates.

questions.question: How is a module added to a product image?

answers.text: Listing it in PRODUCT_PACKAGES in the product makefile
Any module defined in an Android.bp is installed automatically
Adding it to the root Android.bp

questions.explanation: Product configuration is still make-based; PRODUCT_PACKAGES selects what gets installed.

questions.question: What does the 'required' property do?

answers.text: Installs the listed modules whenever this module is installed
Adds the modules to the compile classpath
Fails the build if they are missing in out/

questions.explanation: 'required' is about installation, not linking. Use static_libs/shared_libs/libs for dependencies.

questions.question: Module names in Soong must be…

answers.text: unique across the tree, unless soong_namespace is used

questions.explanation: soong_namespace allows the same module name in different namespaces, e.g. for different devices.

questions.question: Which mechanism lets Android.bp react to product-specific configuration without conditionals?
questions.explanation: Product makefiles set SOONG_CONFIG_* variables; a custom module type maps them to properties.

questions.question: Which module type imports a prebuilt APK?
questions.explanation: android_app_import can keep or replace the signature (presigned / certificate).

questions.question: Are glob patterns like "src/**/*.java" supported in srcs?

answers.text: No, every file must be listed

questions.explanation: Globs are supported; Soong re-runs when the set of matching files changes.

questions.question: What does the visibility property control?

answers.text: Which other modules/packages may depend on this module
Whether the app is visible in the launcher
Which partitions can read the files

questions.explanation: Examples: ["//visibility:public"], ["//visibility:private"] or specific package paths.

questions.question: In Android 14+, what format does the lunch target use?
questions.explanation: The release configuration (e.g. trunk_staging) was added to support trunk-stable development.

questions.question: Which statements about Kati are correct?

answers.text: It processes Android.mk files and product makefiles
It outputs Ninja files that are combined with Soong's

questions.explanation: Kati is a make clone that emits Ninja. Soong and Kati outputs are combined into one Ninja build.
